title: The data and formula engine behind every dashboard

say: The data and formula engine behind every dashboard.
This is the video for module one of Advanced Excel and Dashboards.
At advanced level, the hard part of Excel is rarely the formula. It is the shape of the data. Many workbooks look neat on screen but are built like a paper notebook.

say: One row is one record: one sale, one payment. Never mix records with subtotals.

panel.heading: The rules of tidy data
items: One row = one record, no subtotal rows
One column = one kind of information
One header row, no merged cells
No blank rows or columns inside the data
Numbers as numbers, dates as dates

say: One column holds one kind of information. Do not write 12 bags at 14,500 in a single cell.

say: SUMIFS puts what to add up first, then pairs of where to look and what to look for. The older SUMIF puts the sum range last. Mixing them up is a classic error.
Tola keeps the dates, product and town in cells, so one formula can answer many questions. She never types a date inside the quotes.

card.title: SUMIFS: layer mash in Oyo, in March

say: To test it, she filters the Table by hand. Five rows remain: 174,000, 290,000, 145,000, 87,000 and 232,000.

card.title: SUMIFS: layer mash in Oyo, in March

say: They add up to 928,000. Her SUMIFS cell shows 928,000, so the formula is right. Change the product cell and the answer updates instantly.

say: VLOOKUP without its last argument uses approximate match. On an unsorted list it can return a wrong price with no error at all. Always end it with FALSE.

panel.heading: VLOOKUP versus XLOOKUP

say: XLOOKUP is safer, and its match mode minus 1 handles tiers. A rep with 760,000 naira of sales gets the 500,000 tier at 3 percent, so 22,800 naira commission.
XLOOKUP needs Excel 2021, 2024 or Microsoft 365. For 2016 or 2019, use INDEX with MATCH.

say: Build every pivot from the named Table, so new rows are included. If it shows Count of Amount, some cells are text. Fix the data first.

panel.heading: A pivot that answers three questions
items: Insert a PivotTable from the named Table
Group dates by both Months and Years
Add Amount three times with Show Values As
Refresh All after every data change

say: Group by both Months and Years, or January 2024 and January 2025 get added together.

say: Add Amount as a plain sum, then as percent of grand total, then as percent difference from the previous month. In one example, layer mash was 50 percent of sales, and March grew by 19.6 percent.

say: Remember. Tidy data first. Name every Table. SUMIFS puts the sum range first. Use exact matches. And test every formula against a check you did by hand.

panel.heading: What to keep from this module
items: One row per record, no merged cells
Press Ctrl+T and name every Table
SUMIFS puts the sum range first
End VLOOKUP with FALSE, or use XLOOKUP
Test formulas with a hand-filtered check
